question.text: Complex <math> <mtext>X</mtext> </math> of composition <math><mtext>Cr</mtext><msub><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><mtext>C</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>l</mtext></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></mrow></msub></math> has a spin only magnetic moment of <math> <mrow> <mtext>3</mtext><mtext>.83</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>BM</mtext></mrow> </math>. It reacts with <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mtext>N</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>O</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> and shows geometrical isomerism. The IUPAC nomenclature of <math> <mtext>X</mtext> </math> is

solution.text:
This compound can be identified and named as follows
CrH2O6Cln
As μcomplexspin=3.8 B.M. =n(n+2)
On solving n=3
Oxidation No. of Cr=+3
As compound also shows Geometrical isomerism so it will be [CrH2O)4Cl2Cl.2H2O
It is named as → Tetraaquadichloridochromium(III)chloride dihydrate
